name: lightbox-grid
title: Lightbox Grid
description: A compact grid of rounded nature photos where the first tile spans four cells. Any thumbnail opens into a full-window viewer with arrows, a counter and a caption, and can be swiped or dragged back into place.
use: A page shows a handful of photos and each should open large without losing its place.
avoid: Large galleries: every photo mounts in the grid at once, so dozens of tiles mean dozens of image loads.
a11y: Tiles are labelled buttons, focus is trapped in the viewer, Escape and arrows work, and reduced motion skips the flight. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: Six rounded photo tiles pack tightly on black, with one large landscape image filling a two-by-two square on the left and five smaller portrait and landscape photos beside it. The open view centres one photo on a dark backdrop, with a counter and close at top right, round arrows at the sides and a small caption below.
behaves: Tapping a tile sends that same photo flying from its slot to the middle of the screen, growing and uncropping as it goes. Inside, a sideways swipe steps to the next photo, pulling down shrinks the image and flies it home, and Escape, arrows or the buttons close it.
customise: The images array is the content prop; spacing, margins, spring timings and the grid shape are fixed in the source.
weight: light: Six photos plus motion springs during open and close; nothing runs while the grid is idle.
